description: Canonical searchQueryIndex test vectors. Every Tracive SDK (Kotlin, Flutter, Swift, React Native) and the Tracive API MUST produce byte-identical output for these inputs. This file is vendored verbatim into each SDK repository and is the anti-drift contract between them. The Tracive API runs the same file through its own key builder.

derivedFrom.authority: Generated by executing the Tracive API's own canonical key normalizer, not transcribed by hand. If an SDK disagrees with a vector here, the SDK is wrong.
derivedFrom.note: The server also folds caller-supplied keys on the read path, so a key differing only in casing or whitespace still resolves. SDKs fold locally anyway: the folded key is also the local cache key, and an unfolded key would split one entity into several cache entries.

rules.PHONE: PHONE_<value>. Strip every character that is not a digit, preserving a single leading '+'. No case folding (digits only). SDKs additionally REJECT anything that is not E.164 after stripping (^\+[1-9]\d{6,14}$) — the server does not reconcile a local-format number against its E.164 form, so a local number silently becomes a different entity and the miss is still billed.
rules.EMAIL: EMAIL_<value>. Unicode NFC, then lowercase, then trim (in that order). SDKs additionally REJECT a value containing no '@' (reason not_an_email): the server performs no shape validation, so such a key is looked up, missed and billed.
rules.BANK_IBAN: BANK_IBAN_<accountId>. accountId: uppercase, then remove every whitespace character and ASCII hyphen. Note: uppercase happens BEFORE stripping, and NFC is NOT applied.
rules.BANK_COUNTRY: BANK_<country>_<bankCode>_<accountId>. country: uppercase+trim, must be ISO 3166-1 alpha-3. bankCode: NFC, uppercase, trim, then remove every underscore (the id is split on '_', so an underscore would corrupt the parse). accountId: same fold as BANK_IBAN.
rules.BANK_SHORT_CODE: Resolve bankShortCode to a bankCode through the vendored bank-codes.json table (countries[country].shortCode), then fold exactly as BANK_COUNTRY. The country is validated first (country_not_alpha3 wins). Lookup key: NFC, uppercase, then remove every whitespace character (JavaScript \s) and every '.' and '-'. Exact match first; if there is none and the folded code is all ASCII digits, match it with leading zeros removed (regex ^0+(?=\d), so '000' becomes '0') against the table's all-digit codes with the same removal. No match: reject unknown_bank_code. Never build a key from an unresolved code - the server answers such a request with 400 instead of billing a miss. The table must be a real map: 'constructor' and '__proto__' are misses.
rules.BANK_BIC: Resolve bic through countries[country].bic, then fold exactly as BANK_COUNTRY. NFC, uppercase, remove every whitespace character (JavaScript \s); the result must match ^[A-Z]{4}[A-Z]{2}[A-Z0-9]{2}([A-Z0-9]{3})?$; look up its first 8 characters within the given country only. Malformed or absent: reject unknown_bank_code.
rules.CRYPTO: CRYPTO_<chain>_<address>. chain: NFC, uppercase, trim. address: trim, then lowercase IF AND ONLY IF it matches ^0x[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ (an EVM address). Base58 addresses are case-sensitive and must NOT be folded.
rules.USERNAME: USERNAME_<platform>_<handle>. platform: NFC, uppercase, trim. handle: NFC, lowercase, trim. A leading '@' is NOT stripped — the server preserves it, so stripping it client-side would build a key that misses.
rules.QRIS_PAYLOAD: QRIS_<NMID>, read from a QRIS payload (the text a QR decoder returns). Trim tab, LF, CR, space and U+00A0 from both ends. It must start with '000201', else not_a_qris. Read it as TLV: a 2-digit tag, a 2-digit length counted in UTF-16 code units, then the value; a tag or length that is not 2 ASCII digits, or a value past the end, is not_a_qris. The last TLV must be tag 63 with a 4-character value, else not_a_qris. Its value must equal, case-insensitively, CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, no reflection, no final xor) over the UTF-8 bytes of everything before those 4 characters ('6304' included), as 4 upper-case hex digits; else qris_crc_mismatch. A repeated tag keeps its first value. NMID = tag 51, sub-tag 02, folded as QRIS_NMID; no NMID is qris_no_nmid. Criteria = tag 51 sub-tag 03 when, upper-cased, it is one of UMI, UKE, UME, UBE; otherwise (absent or any other value) sub-tag 03 of the first merchant account template (tags 26-45, in tag order) that has a sub-tag 00, by the same test. Anything but UMI or UKE is qris_not_indexed. A template whose value is not TLV inside reads as having no sub-tags. Static or dynamic (tag 01) does not matter here. Checks run in this order: not_a_qris, qris_crc_mismatch, qris_no_nmid, qris_not_indexed.
rules.QRIS_NMID: QRIS_<NMID>. Remove every tab, LF, CR, space and U+00A0 (anywhere, not only the edges), upper-case, and the result must match ^ID[0-9]{13}$ with ASCII digits; else not_an_nmid.
rules.QRIS_PAN: QRIS_<PAN>. Remove every tab, LF, CR, space and U+00A0. 18 ASCII digits is the PAN. 19 ASCII digits whose Luhn check passes (over all 19) folds to its first 18. Anything else is not_a_pan. The server maps a PAN to its NMID after the charge; a PAN it has not seen answers as a miss.

crossLanguageSemantics.$comment: The Tracive API folds keys with JavaScript string semantics. To be byte-identical you must reimplement those, NOT your platform's defaults. Every item below was verified by executing the reference implementation.

trimSet.note: JS String.prototype.trim() strips EXACTLY this set. Hand-write this character class — do not use your platform's trim().
trimSet.platformTraps: Kotlin Regex("\\s") is ASCII-only and Kotlin trim() does not strip U+FEFF. Swift/ICU NSRegularExpression \s omits U+000B and U+FEFF. Dart's trim() follows Unicode WhiteSpace, which differs at U+FEFF.

digitSet.note: JS \D is exactly [^0-9] (ASCII). Arabic-Indic and other Unicode digits are STRIPPED, never converted.
digitSet.platformTraps: ICU \d is Unicode Nd, so an NSRegularExpression phone normalizer would KEEP Arabic-Indic digits the backend removes. Filter on ASCII 0-9 explicitly.

caseMapping.note: JS toLowerCase()/toUpperCase() are locale-INVARIANT full case mappings and can change string length.
caseMapping.platformTraps: Kotlin: use uppercase()/lowercase() with NO Locale argument (uppercase(Locale.getDefault()) breaks under the Turkish locale). Swift: uppercased()/lowercased(), never a locale variant. Dart: toUpperCase()/toLowerCase().

crossLanguageSemantics.nfcScope: NFC is applied to email addresses, usernames, and every CODE field — the social/chain platform code AND the bank code. It is NOT applied to bank account ids, crypto addresses or phone numbers. Verified by execution: a bank code carrying a combining mark composes before uppercasing, which is length-changing, so an implementation that skips NFC here builds a key that cannot match.
crossLanguageSemantics.foldOrder: Order is part of the contract. email/username: NFC -> lowercase -> trim. platform/chain/bank code: NFC -> uppercase -> trim. bank account: uppercase -> strip [\s-] (NO separate trim). crypto address: trim -> conditional lowercase. Reordering changes output on edge inputs.
crossLanguageSemantics.phoneFolding: The server folds PHONE on the read path, but SDKs MUST fold it client-side regardless: the folded key is also the local cache key, so an unfolded one would split a single entity across several cache entries and defeat the cache-hit path entirely. Never rely on the server to fold on your behalf.

documentIdGuard.$comment: Applied server-side to the FOLDED key (folding runs first because case mapping is not length-preserving). Mirror it client-side so a doomed key never costs a credit.

cases.why: The reserved pattern is ^__.*__$ and '.' does not match a newline without the s flag, so the server ACCEPTS this key. A client implementing the rule as startsWith('__') && endsWith('__') is stricter than the server and falsely rejects it. Verified by execution.

notImplemented.DOMAIN: The Tracive API indexes exactly six identifier types: PHONE, EMAIL, BANK, CRYPTO, USERNAME and QRIS. There is no DOMAIN type, so a DOMAIN_<host> key would match nothing — and a miss is still billed. SDKs MUST NOT expose a domain() query builder. If a DOMAIN type is ever added it will arrive as a new input.type value, which is not a breaking change.

vectors.why: Formatting punctuation is stripped so every printed form collapses to one key.
Decomposed 'e' + U+0301 combining acute must NFC-compose to U+00E9, otherwise one address indexes as two entities.
A dashed and an undashed account number are the same account.
The id is split on '_', so underscores are stripped from the bank code defensively.
IBANs are printed in groups of four; the spaces are presentational.
EIP-55 checksum casing is presentational; record keys are case-sensitive.
Base58 is case-SENSITIVE: lowercasing yields a different, invalid address. Base58 excludes '0', so it can never collide with the 0x EVM test.
bech32 is not folded: its regex admits only the lowercase form, so the other case never reaches the index.
The server does NOT strip a leading '@'; it only folds NFC, case and whitespace. Stripping it client-side would build a key that misses a report filed with the '@'.
USERNAME is split on the FIRST underscore only, so underscores in the handle round-trip.
JS trim() strips U+00A0. A bank-statement or PDF paste carries NBSP. Kotlin trim() also strips it, but a hand-rolled ASCII-only class would not.
JS trim() does NOT strip U+200B (ZWSP). Mirroring the server means keeping it, even though the key then misses — matching the server is the contract, not guessing what the user meant.
U+0130 lowercases to 'i' + U+0307 COMBINING DOT ABOVE under the locale-invariant mapping. Passing a Turkish locale would produce plain 'i' and a different key.
The /[\s-]/ class includes U+00A0; Kotlin's Regex("\\s") is ASCII-only and would leave the NBSP in.
Case mapping is length-changing: 'ß' uppercases to 'SS'. This is also why the 1500-byte guard must run AFTER folding.
Underscores are deliberately kept in the account (the id is split on '_' but everything past the bank code is rejoined).
JS \D is ASCII [^0-9], so U+0669 ARABIC-INDIC NINE is REMOVED, not converted to '9'. An ICU-based \d port would keep it and build a different key.

The EVM test regex requires a LOWERCASE '0x' prefix, so an uppercase '0X' address is not folded. The write path applies the same rule, so the two sides still agree — mirror it exactly rather than 'fixing' it.

The bank code goes through the same NFC-then-uppercase fold as a platform code. 'A'+U+0301 composes to U+00C1, which is length-changing. An implementation that reads nfcScope as excluding bank codes drifts here, and nothing else in the fixture catches it.
A national bank code resolves to Tracive's bankCode, so the key is the one bankCode BCA builds.
Partners that store the code as a number send 14 for 014. Leading zeros are optional.
Every JavaScript \s character is removed, U+00A0 included. A platform whose default whitespace class omits U+00A0 drifts here.
Some national codes are letters (Nepal's NCHL short codes). They are upper-cased before the lookup.
A bank's second code (here HSBC's second legal entity in Singapore) resolves to the same bankCode.
An 11-character BIC is folded to its first 8 characters; case does not matter.
A second legal entity's BIC resolves to the same bankCode.
The key is the NMID in tag 51 sub-tag 02, never the PAN or the merchant name.
A dynamic QR is never indexed itself, but the UMI or UKE merchant behind it can be indexed from its static QR, so the check is allowed (the Tracive app keeps its button for it too).
Only tab, LF, CR, space and U+00A0 are trimmed from the payload edges.
The CRC compares case-insensitively.
With no criteria in tag 51, the first merchant account template (26-45, in tag order) that has a GUID gives it; criteria compare case-insensitively.
Unknown tags are skipped.
A repeated tag keeps its first value; a template that is not TLV inside reads as empty.
TLV lengths count UTF-16 code units (JavaScript String.length) while the CRC runs over the UTF-8 bytes; U+00C9 is one unit and two bytes.
A tag 51 criteria that is not one of UMI, UKE, UME, UBE counts as absent, so the merchant account template's criteria decides.
An emoji is two UTF-16 code units in a TLV length. Swift must measure the utf16 view, not Characters or unicodeScalars.
An NMID is upper-cased and loses every tab, LF, CR, space and U+00A0, wherever they sit.
The server maps a PAN to its NMID after the charge; the SDK cache keeps the PAN key apart from the NMID key.
Receipts print 19 digits: the 18 of the QR plus a Luhn check digit, dropped only when it checks out.
The Luhn check doubles every second digit counting from the check digit, which is not doubled. Doubling the other half gives 7 here, so 9360091500123456787 is not this PAN.

rejected.why: The server does not up-convert a local number to E.164 (it cannot know the dial code at that layer). Sending it would create a different entity and be billed as a miss.
E.164 country codes never start with 0.
The server would up-convert ID to IDN, but the SDK requires alpha-3 so the local cache key matches the server key exactly. Callers must pass alpha-3.
The write path drops a row with an empty account id, so such a key can never hit.
A record key cannot contain '/'. Guarded before the request is sent.
Keys matching __.*__ are reserved.
A key like CRYPTO_ETH_ can only miss, and a miss is billed. Previously rejected with the generic empty-value token, which made two different mistakes indistinguishable to a caller.
USERNAME__scammerx cannot match any stored key. Same reasoning as crypto-empty-address.

The server does not validate email shape: EMAIL_budi is a legal record key, so it is looked up, missed, and billed. Client-side rejection is the only thing that prevents the charge - the same protection phone() already gives via its E.164 check. A value with no '@' cannot be an address, so this rejects nothing a caller could legitimately have meant.
The server rejects a code it does not list with 400 instead of billing a miss, so the SDK rejects it before sending.
A lookup on a plain JavaScript object would find an inherited member here. The table must be a real map.
A BIC is looked up within the given country only.
The country is validated before the code is looked up.
The QR was edited or misread. Tell the user the QR is not intact rather than calling it unreported.
Only UMI and UKE QRIS are ever indexed (medium and large businesses never are), so this check could only be a billed miss.
A criteria that is absent or unknown is never indexed either.
A known criteria in tag 51 wins over the merchant account template's, even when the template says UMI.
An NMID that is not ID plus 13 digits reads as none.
U+2003 is not in the NMID space set (tab, LF, CR, space, U+00A0), unlike JavaScript trim().
A 19th digit that is not the Luhn digit means the number is not this PAN.
7 is the check digit only if the wrong half of the digits is doubled.
Only ASCII 0-9 are digits here, as in JavaScript [0-9].
